text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Route53 weighted-routing anomaly detected for api.redwood.example — increased 5xxs and connection timeouts from clients in ap-south-1 and eu-west-1. Auto-alert triggered: >5% 5xx on global LB for 10m :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): diving in. seeing p95 spike to ~1.2s and 504s from ELB health checks. Correlating with recent Route53 change? :thinking_face:

bob (network): checking DNS propagation graphs — some resolved IPs for ap-south still point at old ELB after the rollout at 09:12 UTC. Looks like weights didn't fully apply in a subset of resolvers (ISP caching).

claire (sre): impact: ~3% of requests hitting an instance group with degraded network path; error budget at risk for a few customers. Repro steps: curl -v api.redwood.example from eu-west-1 shows TLS handshake sometimes times out.

alice (oncall): quick mitigation options: 1) push weight to healthy region (us-west-2) 2) enable fallback host header routing 3) advertise via CDN bypass. I'd push weight first to reduce blast radius. Thoughts?

bob (network): +1 for weight shift. If propagation lag persists, we can also create a temporary CNAME for the affected cohort and change TTL. Current TTL was 60s but some resolvers are ignoring it.

dave (support): customers reporting increase in API errors for inference endpoints. I'm drafting an external note to status with ETA for mitigation. Need exact impact numbers. Can SRE confirm percent of traffic failing?

claire (sre): from global metrics: 97.2% success, errors concentrated in ap-south/eu-west resolvers. Estimated 3% affected, spike started 2023-11-12T09:15:00Z (approx).

alice (oncall): executing AWS CLI change to shift Route53 weights to us-west-2 (95%) to drain problematic backends. command:

```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE --change-batch '{
  "Changes": [
    {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{
      "Name":"api.redwood.example.",
      "Type":"A",
      "SetIdentifier":"us-west-2",
      "Weight":95,
      "ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.14.23.11"}]
    }},
    {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{
      "Name":"api.redwood.example.",
      "Type":"A",
      "SetIdentifier":"ap-south-1",
      "Weight":5,
      "ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"13.126.45.6"}]
    }}
  ]
}'
```

alice (oncall): change submitted. Change ID: C5678ROUTE53. Waiting for propagated checks. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-shift-bot: Route53 change C5678ROUTE53 status: INSYNC in 45s.

claire (sre): metrics already showing reduction in errors. p95 back to 280ms after ~90s. Keeping watch.

bob (network): parallel step: started targeted ELB connection drain for ap-south target group to stop new connections to degraded hosts. command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:ap-south-1:... --targets Id=i-0abc...`

dave (support): posted status update: "We are investigating elevated API errors affecting a subset of regions; mitigation in progress, customers may see intermittent timeouts. Updates every 15 minutes." Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2421

emily (engops): adding runbook note: note caching anomalies observed in ISPs ignoring TTL. Recommend followup: contact major ISP peers if recurrence.

alice (oncall): after 8m of watch: errors down to baseline. No new pager alerts. I'll keep the weight adjusted for 30m, then gradually restore to original plan once we confirm stable resolver behavior.

claire (sre): creating incident ticket and collecting artifacts: traceroutes, ELB logs, Route53 change history, resolver logs. Attaching sample curl output below:

```
* curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health
* Connected to 13.126.45.6 (13.126.45.6) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timed out
* Connection failed -> 504
```

alice (oncall): handing off to bob for next 2 hours (on-call rotation). @bob please pick up post-mitigation monitoring and begin RCA when you have bandwidth. :handshake:

bob (network): taking handoff. I'll coordinate with CDN and peering contacts. Next steps: verify DNS resolvers list that still show stale records, capture EDNS client subnet patterns.

dave (support): will keep support channel updated and close interim status once metrics hold for 30m.

alice (oncall): filing short post-incident note in #postmortems and scheduling a 30m follow-up meeting. Preliminary hypothesis: partial resolver noncompliance with TTL during recent weighted rollout caused a split-brain where a small cohort continued to hit degraded ELBs. Mitigation: emergency weight shift + targeted drain.

ops-shift-bot: Incident INC-2421 created and assigned to incidents@redwood. Postmortem owner: bob (network).

bob (network): acknowledged. I'll assemble timeline and include recommendations: increase Route53 health-check redundancy, add per-ISP telemetry for critical hostnames, and consider session affinity tolerant fallbacks.

claire (sre): moving to monitoring watchlist. If anything changes I'll reopen pager. :eyes:

emily (engops): tagging this for product and SRE review. Adding runbook entry: "If weighted propagation lag > 3m, consider emergency weight shift and file ISP ticket."

alice (oncall): resolved for now. closing the active page. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
